exposure: levels of specific fecal microorganisms (e.g., Staphylococcus, Bacteroides)
cohort: 124 full-term infants (88 vaginally delivered and 36 C-section delivered)
finding: Early life gut microbiota composition, particularly Staphylococcus and Bacteroides levels, was associated with weight gain in infants during their first year of life, with variations observed between vaginally and C-section delivered babies.
mod_finding: This study found a significant association between the levels of certain gut microbes and infant weight gain, with differences observed between infants delivered vaginally and those delivered via C-section.
